semantic_checks: Actual rotation is (a*x-b*y,b*x+a*y). The transformed independent variables have factors u=a+i*b and star(u); the real evaluation identities are proved coordinatewise, without imposing conjugacy inside the polynomial ring.

For every support coefficient c!=0, actual circle invariance gives c*u^d0*star(u)^d1=c. Unit norm supplies star(u)*u=1; legitimate cancellation yields u^d0=u^d1 for every unit u. The existing explicit primitive-root separation theorem then gives d0=d1.

Real polynomial equality is transported through the proved inverse coordinate substitutions and real-slice polynomial extensionality. The local version uses a positive real box with infinite sides, not a claim that the real box is complex open.

The actual unit-complex norm condition implies re(u)^2+im(u)^2=1, so the stated real rotation hypothesis supplies exactly the required circle invariance. No invariance of a physical eigenfunction or its polynomial jets is inferred.

Local hrot applies to every original x in the positive real box and every real unit rotation. It explicitly asserts equality even if the rotated point leaves that box; the proof does not claim the box is rotation invariant.

Finite/even/odd radial wrappers derive balanced support and consume the already reviewed literal radial identities, retaining exactly the original Cartesian axis coefficients and all zero-degree/zero-polynomial cases.
limits: These results discharge balanced support from the stated polynomial real rotation invariance. Deriving polynomial invariance from analytic-function invariance or physical inputs is a subsequent obligation.
The local theorem hypothesis is stronger than invariance asserted only when both x and rotated x lie in an arbitrary box; any such application must supply a suitable smaller neighborhood.
Existing pinned Lean/mathlib caches are reused. No isolated dependency source rebuild, numerical algorithm or full R05/Theorem T verification is claimed.
